title: Verafin alum-led Verlo nabs $4.5 million to build AI operating system for wealth managers
html:
Verlo has closed $4.5 million CAD in seed funding to reduce the administrative burden facing wealth managers using AI.

The news: The St. John’s technology startup, which bills itself as “the compliant AI operating system” for independent financial advisors and wealth management firms, announced the round on Monday. Toronto’s Staircase Ventures led with support from returning local backer Pelorus VC and angel investors, including founders and key executives from Canadian tech success story Verafin. The financing brings Verlo’s total funding to $6.5 million. Verlo, which aims to help wealth managers save time on admin work and focus more on growing their businesses without adding operational overhead, plans to put this capital towards product development, hiring, and expansion in the United States.

From the source: “Verlo has the product, team, and traction to win,” Staircase Ventures founder and managing partner Janet Bannister said in a statement. “When we met [founder and CEO] Brent [Pretty], we were immediately impressed by his tenacity, vision, bias for action, and understanding of the nuances of building great products in heavily regulated industries.”

The context: Verafin, which built financial crime detection software for banks and credit unions, sold to US stock exchange Nasdaq in 2020 in a massive, $2.7-billion USD ($3.8-billion CAD) cash deal. That deal was by far Atlantic Canada’s largest-ever tech exit, and still represents one of the country’s overall biggest to date. Like other Newfoundland and Labrador-based tech startups, Verlo’s Verafin connections run deep. Pretty, who launched Verlo in 2024, previously spent nearly five years leading AI workflow automation at Verafin as a product manager both pre- and post-acquisition. The startup’s team also features a number of other former Verafin staff with experience building software for the tightly regulated financial services industry.

Final thought: While legacy wealth management software providers are beginning to introduce AI, Pretty said in many cases, they “feel more like add-ons to existing workflows” than truly integrated, transformative tech. Verlo is betting that it can move the needle even further by ensuring all of its clients’ data is searchable to AI agents.

summary: Staircase Ventures led the St. John’s startup’s round, with backing from Pelorus and Verafin leaders. The post Verafin alum-led Verlo nabs $4.5 million to build AI operating system for wealth managers first appeared on BetaKit .
